title: SIEM Analysis: SSH Scan and Firewall Rule (CM-2026-0087)

fields.incidentName: Retail Payment System Outage — Network Failure
fields.to: All Command and Control Roles; Airport Operations; Public Information Officer; Legal & Compliance
fields.summary: At 10:15, IT confirms a prior overnight SSH scanning attempt from IP 185.220.101.34, detected between 2:00 and 2:15 AM. The scans targeted the airport's perimeter firewall and were blocked by failed authentication. This IP is associated with the CISA-issued advisory TI-2026-0312, a known botnet probing infrastructure. The same IP range was later blocked in a rule change logged at 09:45 by IT Manager Jordan Kelley, identified as CM-2026-0087. The rule was intended to block 185.220.0.0/16 but was applied to the Retail VLAN (10.1.40.0/24) with 'any' source zone and address. This change occurred just two minutes before the first POS terminal failed at 09:47. The rule is now active and potentially causing the network outage affecting 47 retail terminals across Concourses A and B. No further scanning has been detected since 2:15 AM.

keyStatus.label: POS Terminals
keyStatus.value: All offline — no network reach to payment gateway

keyStatus.label: Firewall Rule CM-2026-0087
keyStatus.value: Active — Source: any, Destination: Retail VLAN

actions.text: Initial report from Vendor Manager: 47 retail terminals now cash-only; lines forming in Concourse A.
RetailLink Vendor confirms firmware v4.2.1 pushed at 09:30; terminals online but not reaching gateway.
IT SIEM analysis confirms SSH scan from 185.220.101.34 (TI-2026-0312) occurred at 2:00–2:15 AM; failed access attempts logged.
Firewall rule CM-2026-0087 (intended to block 185.220.0.0/16) confirmed in change log; applied to Retail VLAN (10.1.40.0/24) with 'any' source.

planned: Review full firewall rule set and reverse CM-2026-0087 immediately.
Verify all access control system (ASC) doors in Secured Area are operating under fail-secure mode.
Notify PEO and Legal of potential change management failure.
Begin forensic review of IT Manager Jordan Kelley’s session logs for CM-2026-0087.
issues: Unintended rule CM-2026-0087 remains active — may prevent any recovery until reversed.
No prior peer review of firewall change CM-2026-0087 — violates change management policy.
TSA and FBI have not been notified — potential compliance risk if threat is misclassified.

instructorNote: This inject forces the team to confront the timeline and rule structure. The IT team must now examine the actual firewall rule to detect the misconfiguration. Watch for whether they pivot from scanning to rule review.
